paragraphs.title: Bringing the Ark and Establishing Levitical Service

answers: In the midst of the tent David had pitched for it
easy.explanation: The ark was set in the midst of David’s tent.
easy.q: Where did they place the ark of God?

easy.explanation: The passage names burnt offerings and peace offerings.
easy.q: What offerings did they present before God?

easy.explanation: David appointed certain Levites to minister before the ark.
easy.q: Whom did David appoint to minister before the ark?

answers: He blessed the people in the name of the LORD
He sent the priests to Gibeon
medium.explanation: David blessed the people in the name of the LORD.
medium.q: What did David do after he finished offering the sacrifices?

answers: A loaf of bread, a piece of flesh, and a flagon of wine
medium.explanation: David dealt food and wine to every man and woman.
medium.q: What did David give to every person of Israel?

answers: Guarding the city and building an altar
Judging the people and distributing gifts
Recording, thanking, and praising the LORD
medium.explanation: The Levites were appointed to record, thank, and praise the LORD.
medium.q: What duties were assigned to the Levites before the ark?

answers: The celebration and gifts included all the people
The gifts were given only to musicians
challenge.explanation: The wording shows that both men and women throughout Israel received the gifts.
challenge.q: What does David’s distribution of food to every man and woman show?

answers: Asaph guarded the gate, while the priests distributed food
Asaph made a sound with cymbals, while the priests used trumpets
Asaph offered sacrifices, while the priests played harps
challenge.explanation: Asaph used cymbals, while Benaiah and Jahaziel used trumpets.
challenge.q: Which detail distinguishes Asaph’s service from that of Benaiah and Jahaziel?

answers: As a one-time task without assigned duties
As work done only outside the tent
As organized service involving recording, music, and praise
challenge.explanation: The passage lists specific duties and musical service before the ark.
challenge.q: How is the Levites’ service presented in this passage?

paragraphs.title: The Opening Thanksgiving Song and the Covenant

easy.explanation: David delivered the psalm into the hand of Asaph and his brethren.
easy.q: Into whose hand did David deliver the psalm?

easy.explanation: The song begins, “Give thanks unto the LORD, call upon his name.”
easy.q: Whom does the song call upon the people to thank and call upon?

easy.explanation: The covenant is associated with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
easy.q: Whom does the song mention in connection with the covenant?

medium.explanation: It says, “let the heart of them rejoice that seek the LORD.”
medium.q: What does the song tell the heart of those who seek the LORD to do?

answers: Give thanks, sing, remember, and seek the LORD
Offer sacrifices, make war, and build a city
medium.explanation: The song calls people to give thanks, sing, remember God’s works, and seek Him.
medium.q: What is the main sequence of commands at the beginning of the song?

answers: To recall the covenant and promise given to the fathers
medium.explanation: The song recalls God’s covenant and oath to the patriarchs.
medium.q: Why are Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob mentioned?

answers: Both strengthen awareness of God’s works and promises
challenge.explanation: The song joins remembrance of God’s deeds with remembrance of His continuing covenant.
challenge.q: How are remembering God’s wonders and remembering His covenant related?

answers: Those whom God appointed and sent were not to be harmed
No one was allowed to sing before the ark
challenge.explanation: The warning forbids harming God’s anointed ones and prophets.
challenge.q: What is suggested by “Touch not mine anointed, and do my prophets no harm”?

answers: From the priests to the gatekeepers only
From the ark to the tent only
From those who seek the LORD to Israel and the children of Jacob
challenge.explanation: The song moves from individual seekers to Israel and Jacob’s descendants.
challenge.q: How does the song broaden its focus from individuals to the whole people?

paragraphs.title: A Call for All the Earth to Praise the Lord

easy.explanation: The command is addressed to all the earth.
easy.q: To whom is the command “Sing unto the LORD” addressed?

answers: The LORD’s glory and marvellous works
The names of all the Levites
easy.explanation: They were to declare His glory and marvellous works.
easy.q: What were the people to declare among the heathen?

easy.explanation: The passage repeatedly says that His mercy endureth for ever.
easy.q: What is said about the LORD’s mercy?

answers: He is great, greatly to be praised, and made the heavens
He gave every person a musical instrument
medium.explanation: The song emphasizes His greatness, glory, and creation.
medium.q: Why is the LORD worthy to be praised according to the song?

answers: The heavens and earth rejoice, the sea roars, and the field rejoices
The sea dries up and the field is abandoned
medium.explanation: The heavens, earth, sea, fields, and trees are all described as rejoicing.
medium.q: How does creation respond to the song’s proclamation?

medium.explanation: They were told to give glory and strength, bring an offering, and worship.
medium.q: What were the kindreds of the people told to give unto the LORD?

answers: The gods of the people are idols, but the LORD made the heavens
The gods made the heavens, but the LORD is an idol
The song makes no distinction between them
challenge.explanation: The verse calls the other gods idols and declares that the LORD made the heavens.
challenge.q: What contrast is made between the gods of the people and the LORD?

answers: The world will cease to exist
The world is established securely before the LORD
The sea will cover the whole earth
challenge.explanation: The phrase describes a stable and established world.
challenge.q: What does “the world also shall be stable, that it be not moved” mean in context?

answers: Creation joins in proclaiming the LORD’s kingship
Nature is mentioned only to describe Gibeon
challenge.explanation: The rejoicing heavens, earth, sea, fields, and trees accompany the declaration that the LORD reigns.
challenge.q: How does the joy of nature relate to the announcement that the LORD reigneth?

paragraphs.title: Assigning Duties for the Ark, Gibeon, and the Gatekeepers

easy.explanation: David left Asaph and his brethren before the ark.
easy.q: Whom did David leave to minister before the ark?

answers: Zadok the priest and his brethren the priests
easy.explanation: Zadok and the priests served before the tabernacle at Gibeon.
easy.q: Who was appointed before the tabernacle of the LORD at Gibeon?

easy.explanation: The offerings were made continually in the morning and evening.
easy.q: When were burnt offerings offered upon the altar?

answers: They offered all the burnt offerings
medium.explanation: Obed-edom and Hosah are identified as porters.
medium.q: What was the duty of Obed-edom and Hosah?

answers: To show that the work was divided among different places and duties
To say that the ark was at Gibeon
medium.explanation: The passage describes service before the ark and priestly service at Gibeon.
medium.q: Why is the service at Gibeon mentioned alongside service before the ark?

medium.explanation: Heman and Jeduthun served with trumpets, cymbals, and musical instruments.
medium.q: What did Heman and Jeduthun use in their service?

answers: They followed a regular and ongoing order
They were made only during a celebration
challenge.explanation: “Continually,” together with “morning and evening,” indicates an established routine.
challenge.q: What does the word “continually” suggest about the offerings?

answers: Asaph was a porter and Zadok was a singer
Asaph served before the ark, while Zadok and the priests offered sacrifices at Gibeon
Asaph offered sacrifices at Gibeon, while Zadok guarded the gate
challenge.explanation: Asaph served before the ark, while Zadok and the priests served at Gibeon.
challenge.q: What is the main difference between the duties of Asaph and Zadok?

answers: They are presented as unrelated activities
The service includes both offerings and thanksgiving with music
challenge.explanation: The passage describes sacrifices together with thanksgiving and musical service.
challenge.q: How are song and sacrifice joined in the worship described?

paragraphs.title: The Celebration Ends and the People Return Home

easy.explanation: The verse says that every man departed to his house.
easy.q: Where did all the people go after the celebration?

answers: He returned to bless his house
easy.explanation: David returned to bless his house.
easy.q: What did David do after the people went home?

answers: The beginning of the tent’s construction
The end of the celebration and the people’s return home
easy.explanation: The verse closes the event with the people going home and David returning to his household.
easy.q: What does the final verse describe?

answers: David blessed his house, and then the people returned
The people returned home, and then David returned to bless his house
The priests offered sacrifices, and then David appointed Asaph
medium.explanation: The people departed first, and David then returned to bless his house.
medium.q: What is the order of events in the verse?

answers: The public event ended and family life continued
The people remained before the ark
medium.explanation: The verse moves from the public celebration back to the home.
medium.q: What can be understood from the movement from the public gathering to David’s house?

answers: The continuation of joy and blessing in the family setting
The transfer of David’s office to Asaph
medium.explanation: David carried the spirit of blessing from the public event into his household.
medium.q: What does David’s blessing of his house express?

answers: It brings the participants from the public gathering back to their homes
It moves the ark to Gibeon
challenge.explanation: The conclusion shows the people dispersing and David returning home.
challenge.q: How does the ending complete the celebration described in the chapter?

answers: The celebration ended in an orderly way
challenge.explanation: Their return home indicates a proper conclusion to the celebration.
challenge.q: What may be inferred from the people returning to their houses?

answers: At first David blessed the people, and at the end he blessed his house
In both places only the priests blessed
At first the people blessed David, and at the end David blessed the nations
challenge.explanation: David first blessed the people and later returned to bless his household.
challenge.q: What connection exists between the blessing at the beginning and the blessing at the end?
